decisions.context: Cameras must detect defects while production lines may have no network access. The brief gives no specific latency target.

alternatives.label: On-device edge inference
pros: Disconnected operation: inference runs on the device
Infrastructure cost: avoids a continuous serving service
cons: Deployment effort: distribute models to devices
Device capacity: constrained by local hardware

alternatives.label: Model-as-a-service deployment
pros: Model updates: central serving simplifies rollout
Device capacity: inference uses server resources
cons: Disconnected operation: requires network access
Infrastructure cost: requires serving infrastructure

decisions.rationale: Disconnected operation decides the choice: inference stays available without a network connection. This gives up the simpler central model rollout of a service; the evidence supports edge placement but does not establish its cost or device requirements.
consequences: Plan a reliable way to distribute model updates to devices.
Validate inference performance and resource use on target hardware.

decisions.context: The model is retrained weekly from newly labelled images. The system needs a repeatable way to start that work.

alternatives.label: Schedule-based retraining trigger
pros: Weekly cadence: directly supports recurring runs
Small team: avoids manual run initiation
cons: New labels: schedule may run before data is ready
Model quality: schedule alone does not detect degradation

alternatives.label: Performance- or drift-based retraining trigger
pros: Model quality: can react to degradation or drift
Compute cost: can avoid unnecessary scheduled runs
cons: Weekly cadence: does not ensure weekly training
Small team: requires monitoring and trigger maintenance

decisions.rationale: The stated weekly cadence decides the choice: schedule retraining weekly, gated on the new labels being available. This gives up automatic response to drift between runs; the design space also supports automated retraining, with evidence in MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning.
consequences: Make label availability a prerequisite for each scheduled run.
Budget for retraining even when model quality has not changed.

decisions.decision: How should candidates be checked before release?
decisions.context: Weekly retraining produces a candidate that may replace the model running on cameras. A repeatable quality check is needed before promotion.

alternatives.label: Offline evaluation pipeline
pros: Weekly updates: repeatable evaluation before deployment
Production quality: tests candidates against held-out data
cons: Small team: requires a maintained evaluation pipeline
Production quality: depends on representative held-out data

alternatives.label: Metric-driven candidate model evaluation
pros: Production quality: compares candidates on selected metrics
Small team: makes promotion criteria explicit
cons: Weekly updates: still needs a maintained evaluation process
Production quality: metric choice may miss other defects

decisions.rationale: Production quality decides the choice: evaluate each weekly candidate against held-out labelled data before promotion. This gives up the broader comparison of multiple candidates described by metric-driven evaluation; the two values can also be combined, and the design space marks evaluation choices as affecting production monitoring outcomes.
consequences: Maintain a held-out dataset separate from training data.
Define a promotion rule using inspection-quality metrics.

decisions.decision: How should model updates reach devices?
decisions.context: Retrained models must be pushed to devices, where an update can affect production inspection. Release automation offers staged rollout and rollback options.

alternatives.label: Progressive release automation with rollback
pros: Production continuity: supports staged updates and rollback
Small team: automates repeatable release steps
cons: Production continuity: staged rollout adds release complexity
Small team: rollback requires version and device coordination

alternatives.label: Environment-gated deployment automation
pros: Production continuity: validation gates precede production
Small team: automates environment-specific release steps
cons: Safe weekly updates: no explicit rollback capability
Production continuity: gates can slow a weekly release

decisions.rationale: Production continuity decides the choice: staged rollout with rollback limits the impact of a bad model update. This gives up the simpler release flow of environment gates alone and adds coordination across device versions; Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture and Azure Machine Learning describe this approach.
consequences: Track which model version each device is running.
Provide a tested path to restore a prior model version.

decisions.decision: How should retraining and evaluation steps be coordinated?
decisions.context: Weekly retraining and pre-release evaluation require ordered, repeatable workflow steps. Manual execution may reduce initial setup, but adds recurring work for a small team.

alternatives.label: Orchestrated ML pipeline
pros: Weekly cadence: connects repeatable workflow stages
Reproducibility: standardizes preparation, training, and evaluation
cons: Infrastructure budget: orchestration adds setup and operations
Small team: pipeline changes require maintenance

alternatives.label: Manual script-driven workflow
pros: Infrastructure budget: avoids orchestration infrastructure
Small team: simple when workflows are infrequent
cons: Weekly cadence: recurring manual steps consume team time
Reproducibility: execution depends on consistent operator practice

decisions.rationale: The weekly cadence decides the choice: orchestrate preparation, training, evaluation, and deployment so the recurring workflow is repeatable. This gives up the lower initial operational burden of manual scripts. The checked design point—edge inference, weekly schedule trigger, offline evaluation, progressive release, and an orchestrated pipeline—has no attesting source combination; a rival swapping in service inference and drift-triggered retraining also has no attesting sources, so the combination remains an informed design choice rather than an attested one.
consequences: Maintain the pipeline definition alongside model code.
Allocate time for pipeline setup and operational ownership.

uncovered: The brief does not specify the inference latency target or camera hardware constraints.
The training compute location and infrastructure for weekly retraining are unspecified.
The model family, image preprocessing, and inspection-quality metrics are unspecified.
The process for producing labels and retaining or versioning images is unspecified.
The device update transport, connectivity recovery, and security controls are unspecified.
The chosen design point is unattested as a combination in the design space; the checked rival combination was also unattested.
